home-remodeling.local_heading: Two kinds of homes, one standard
intro_paragraphs: Sunny Isles Beach housing splits cleanly in two. Along Collins Avenue it is towers: flow-through residences at the Estates at Acqualina, Turnberry Ocean Club, and Jade Signature, plus 1970s-era buildings like Winston Towers where original interiors are overdue for a gut. West of Collins, Golden Shores and Atlantic Isle hold the city's single-family stock — 1950s and '60s houses on canal and bay lots, many still wearing their original layouts. High-end owners in both camps end up doing the same thing: taking the unit or the house down to structure and rebuilding it around how they actually live.

Every permit here is issued by the City of Sunny Isles Beach Building Department, which handles plan review, revisions, and inspections through a fully digital portal. Condo work adds a second gate before the city ever sees a drawing: association approval packages, insurance certificates, service-elevator reservations, and enforced work-hour windows. In Golden Shores, FEMA flood zones make the substantial-improvement math matter on older homes, and every window, door, and roof assembly needs Miami-Dade product approval for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. We handle all of it, in the right order.

A remodel at this level is mostly logistics and discipline. PGX gives you a fixed written scope before demolition, a supervisor on site every working day, and finish protection that treats a marble lobby or a downstairs neighbor's ceiling as part of the job. One accountable team carries the project from estimate through final inspection and warranty — 20-plus years building in South Florida, more than 150 remodels and additions delivered, every one of them permitted and inspected.

faqs.q: Do you remodel condo units in Sunny Isles Beach towers?
faqs.a: Yes — full-unit renovations are a core part of our work here. Every building has its own process: an approval package for the association, certificates of insurance, contractor registration, service-elevator bookings, and strict work hours. We have those requirements resolved before demolition is scheduled, protect the common areas like they are part of your unit, and keep the property manager informed so your project stays welcome in the building.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home or full-unit remodel take?
faqs.a: Be skeptical of anyone who quotes a number before seeing drawings. In towers, association review adds weeks before the city's digital permit review even begins, and elevator access meters how fast material moves. A genuine gut renovation typically runs several months to a year depending on scope and finish level. What we commit to is a written schedule tied to a fixed scope, updated honestly as the job progresses.

faqs.q: What does the FEMA 50 percent rule mean for my Golden Shores house?
faqs.a: If the cost of improvements to an older home exceeds half of the structure's market value, federal flood rules require bringing the whole building into compliance with current elevation standards. On a barrier island like Sunny Isles Beach, that math can reshape a project, so we run the valuation numbers with you at the very start — before design fees, not after — and scope the remodel accordingly.

faqs.q: Does my building's milestone inspection affect my renovation?
faqs.a: It can. Florida now requires milestone structural inspections and structural integrity reserve studies for older condo buildings, and associations in the middle of concrete restoration or facade work often restrict unit renovations, elevator use, or balcony access during that period. We check where your building stands before committing to a schedule, and we sequence interior work around building projects rather than fighting them.

faqs.q: How much does a high-end remodel cost in Sunny Isles Beach?
faqs.a: It depends on scope, structure, and finish level, and any honest answer starts there. We are a high-end contractor, not the low bid — the value we offer is a fixed written scope, licensed and insured execution, and a number that does not drift once work begins. After a walk-through we will give you a real estimate for your unit or house, not a teaser figure designed to win a phone call.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodeling, Sunny Isles Beach — Miami | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchens for Sunny Isles Beach condos and Golden Shores homes. Cabinetry, stone, and permits handled by one licensed GC. Estimates at (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters, and rebuilt layouts for Sunny Isles Beach residences — permitted through the city, cleared with your association where one exists, and supervised daily by PGX Builders Group, Lic. CGC1539072.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Kitchens for towers and canal-front houses
intro_paragraphs: Kitchens in this city come with context. Tower residences at Jade Signature, Muse, and the Ritz-Carlton Residences were delivered with perfectly respectable builder kitchens that owners routinely replace with something personal — a larger island, integrated European appliances, stone with actual movement. In Golden Shores and on Atlantic Isle, the kitchen is often the last original room in a 1950s or '60s house, walled off from the water view the lot was bought for. Both jobs end the same way: a kitchen designed around the person cooking, not around a floor plan somebody else chose.

The City of Sunny Isles Beach Building Department reviews kitchen renovation permits digitally, and the drawings matter. Relocating appliances, gas, or plumbing in a tower means working within the building's risers and stacks, with association sign-off secured before the city's. Anything touching the envelope carries Miami-Dade product-approval requirements for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. In condo buildings, slab penetrations and wet-area changes get reviewed closely — which is exactly how it should be when your new drain line runs above someone else's dining room.

Shop drawings for the cabinetry, slabs approved in person before cutting, and a supervisor on site daily, including the morning the stone rides the service elevator: that is how PGX runs a kitchen. The scope is fixed in writing before demolition, and one licensed team owns everything from rough-in to final inspection, so the lighting plan, the millwork, and the inspection card all agree with each other.

faqs.q: Can I move my sink or appliances in a Sunny Isles Beach condo?
faqs.a: Often yes, within limits set by the building's plumbing risers, drain stacks, and slab construction. Some relocations are simple; others require routing that the association will scrutinize, and a few are genuinely not worth the cost. We assess feasibility against the building's as-built conditions before you spend money on design, so the kitchen you fall for is one that can actually be built in your stack.

faqs.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take in Sunny Isles Beach?
faqs.a: Cabinetry lead times usually set the calendar, not construction. Custom and European lines take months to fabricate, so we sequence association approval and the city's digital permit review during that window, then demolish only when materials are confirmed. Site work on a well-planned kitchen is measured in weeks, and living without a kitchen is unpleasant enough that we do not start it prematurely.

faqs.q: Do you handle the condo association paperwork?
faqs.a: Yes, all of it. We prepare the renovation application, provide certificates of insurance and contractor licensing, register our crews with building security, book the service elevator, and follow the building's noise and work-hour rules without being reminded. Property managers in this city see a lot of contractors; we would rather be the one they are glad to see back.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit just to replace cabinets and counters?
faqs.a: A true like-for-like swap with no plumbing, electrical, or wall changes may fall outside permit requirements, but almost no high-end kitchen stops there. The moment outlets move, lighting changes, or a wall opens, the City of Sunny Isles Beach requires a permit — and unpermitted kitchen work has a way of surfacing at resale or in association records. We permit properly and keep the paper trail clean.

faqs.q: What does a custom kitchen cost at this level?
faqs.a: The honest answer is that cabinetry and stone drive the number more than labor does, and both have wide ranges. We build kitchens for owners who care about the difference, so we will not pretend to be the budget option. What you get from PGX is a fixed written price for a defined scope, itemized clearly enough that you can see exactly where the money lives.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling for Sunny Isles Beach, FL Condos & Homes
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Primary-suite bathrooms in Sunny Isles Beach with stone, frameless glass, and waterproofing done right. Licensed GC CGC1539072. Call (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary bathrooms for Sunny Isles Beach residences: stone, frameless glass, and freestanding tubs over waterproofing that actually holds — permitted with the city and supervised daily by a licensed contractor, CGC1539072.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Where a leak is never just yours
intro_paragraphs: In a Sunny Isles Beach tower, the bathroom is the room where risk lives. Owners at Turnberry Ocean Club, the Estates at Acqualina, and the older Collins Avenue buildings redo primary baths for the same reasons — a bigger shower, a freestanding tub, book-matched stone — but a failed shower pan on the 38th floor is an insurance claim, not an inconvenience. Over in Golden Shores and Poinciana Island, the stock is different: baths from the 1950s through the 1980s with original cast-iron drains and tile set by tradesmen long since retired. Either way, the glamour sits on top of the plumbing.

Bath renovation permits go through the City of Sunny Isles Beach Building Department's online system, and the inspections that matter most happen when nothing looks finished — rough plumbing, then the shower-pan flood test before any tile goes down. Condo associations add their own layer: wet areas generally cannot migrate over a downstairs neighbor's dry space, insurance certificates precede demolition, and work hours are enforced. We treat every bit of that as the baseline for doing business here, not as an obstacle to negotiate.

PGX builds bathrooms in the order that keeps them dry: substrate, slope, membrane, test, and only then stone. You get a fixed written scope, a daily on-site supervisor who has seen every way a shower can fail, and protection from the corridor to the closet while we work. Across 20-plus years and more than 150 remodels and additions in South Florida, we have never met a bathroom worth building without that discipline.

faqs.q: Can I enlarge or move my shower in a Sunny Isles Beach condo?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The governing facts are the location of the building's plumbing risers, the slab construction, and the association's rule that wet areas usually cannot expand over a neighbor's bedroom or living space below. We review the building's as-builts and the association's renovation guidelines before design begins, and we will tell you plainly if the layout you want is not achievable in your line.

faqs.q: What waterproofing do you actually use?
faqs.a: Modern bonded membrane systems installed over correctly sloped substrates, with sealed penetrations and a flood test held long enough to mean something — witnessed and documented before tile is permitted to start. The specific product depends on the assembly, but the sequence never changes. It is the least glamorous line item in the budget and the only one that protects all the others.

faqs.q: How long does a bathroom remodel take here?
faqs.a: Association approval and the city's permit review front-load the calendar, and shower glass is templated only after tile is finished, which puts it last by nature. Once materials are on hand, a primary suite is typically a matter of weeks on site rather than months. We would rather quote you a real schedule after seeing the space than a flattering one before.

faqs.q: Will my downstairs neighbor be affected by the work?
faqs.a: They will hear demolition during permitted hours; that part is physics. What they should never experience is water. That is why the pan is flood-tested before tile, penetrations are sealed, and our insurance certificates are on file with the association before the first hammer swings. Protecting the unit below is not a courtesy in a tower — it is the actual job.

faqs.q: Is it worth pulling a permit for a bathroom remodel?
faqs.a: It is not optional. Plumbing and electrical changes require a permit from the City of Sunny Isles Beach, and in a condominium the association will demand proof of one anyway. Unpermitted wet-area work is precisely what turns up in resale inspections and estoppel files, at the worst possible moment. We permit everything we build, which is why we can warranty everything we build.

home-additions.h1: The square footage you are missing
home-additions.hero_sub: PGX designs and builds additions for Sunny Isles Beach's single-family streets — engineered for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, permitted through the city, and supervised every working day by a licensed GC, CGC1539072.
home-additions.local_heading: Room to grow west of Collins
intro_paragraphs: Nobody adds a wing to the 40th floor. Additions in Sunny Isles Beach happen on the single-family streets west of Collins Avenue, where Golden Shores fills the blocks between 186th and 191st Streets, and gated Atlantic Isle rings its own island with waterfront lots. The originals are mostly two- and three-bedroom houses from the 1950s and '60s — modest footprints on land whose value outgrew them decades ago. Owners who love the location extend toward the canal, go up a story, or convert the garage into a suite rather than trade away a bay view for square footage elsewhere.

Additions run through the City of Sunny Isles Beach Building Department, with structural plans, energy calculations, and Miami-Dade product approvals filed through the city's digital portal; larger projects also get Planning and Zoning attention before a permit is issued. On this barrier island, FEMA flood-zone math shapes the design itself: push an older house past the substantial-improvement threshold and the entire structure must meet current elevation rules. Setbacks, lot coverage, and seawall proximity on Atlantic Isle all get resolved on paper first, which is considerably cheaper than resolving them in the field.

An addition is structural work pretending to be lifestyle work, and PGX treats it that way: foundation assessment before promises, tie-beam and roof connections engineered to current wind code, and a written scope that fixes what the new square footage includes before the first saw cut. Your existing house stays livable and protected while we build. One licensed, insured team — CGC1539072, 20-plus years in South Florida — carries design coordination, permits, inspections, and warranty from start to finish.

faqs.q: Can I add a second story to my Golden Shores house?
faqs.a: Frequently, yes — but the existing foundation and masonry have to prove they can carry it, so we start with a structural evaluation rather than a sketch. Zoning height limits and setbacks apply, and the design has to meet current wind-load requirements throughout. When the numbers work, a second story is often the best way to gain real square footage on a Golden Shores lot without sacrificing the yard.

faqs.q: How does the FEMA 50 percent rule affect additions in Sunny Isles Beach?
faqs.a: If your addition and related improvements exceed half of the existing structure's market value, flood regulations require the whole home to comply with current elevation standards — a very different project. We run that valuation math in the first conversation, and where it is tight, we can phase scope or adjust the design so you know exactly which side of the line the project sits on before spending on engineering.

faqs.q: How long does an addition take from design to move-in?
faqs.a: Plan on a design and permitting phase measured in months — engineering, energy calculations, city review through the digital portal, and Planning and Zoning input on larger projects — followed by a construction phase that depends on size and structure. We give you the honest version at the walk-through, in writing, and we keep the existing house weathertight and livable for as much of the build as the scope allows.

faqs.q: Will my addition need Planning and Zoning review?
faqs.a: Setback, lot-coverage, and height rules apply to every addition, and the City of Sunny Isles Beach routes substantial projects through planning review before building permits are issued. That is not a reason to shrink your ambitions; it is a reason to prepare a complete package the first time. We assemble the drawings, surveys, and calculations so the review has something clean to approve.

faqs.q: Can you make the addition match the original house?
faqs.a: That is the test of whether an addition was built well. We match stucco textures, roof lines, fascia profiles, and window proportions so the house reads as if it was always this size — or, where the owner prefers contrast, we detail the new volume deliberately instead of accidentally. Either way, the transition is designed on paper, not negotiated by the stucco crew on a ladder.

outdoor-living.h1: Outdoor rooms built for salt air
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, and exterior renovations for Sunny Isles Beach properties — engineered for coastal wind, permitted through the city, and built under daily supervision by PGX Builders Group, Lic. CGC1539072.
outdoor-living.local_heading: The backyard is why you're here
intro_paragraphs: Sunny Isles Beach real estate is priced by what is outside the walls, and the outdoor spaces should act like it. In Golden Shores, waterfront lots along North Bay Road carry docks and pool decks that date to a different era of taste; on Atlantic Isle, every home on the island faces the water and lives toward it. Owners here build covered terraces, summer kitchens, and pool surrounds designed for how this climate actually behaves — ten months of outdoor season, salt in the air year-round, and afternoon storms with strong opinions.

Exterior work is permitted work in this city. The City of Sunny Isles Beach Building Department reviews summer kitchens, pergolas, driveways, and structural shade through its digital portal, and anything that has to resist wind — which on this barrier island is everything — needs engineering and Miami-Dade product approvals for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. Flood zones influence slab heights and where equipment can sit, and salt exposure quietly disqualifies half the hardware catalog. We design with the code from day one instead of discovering it at inspection.

PGX builds exteriors with the same discipline as interiors: a fixed written scope, marine-grade materials specified by name, and a supervisor on site daily so the stone deck, the gas line, and the outdoor cabinetry arrive in the correct order. We coordinate re-roofs, stucco, paint, and impact openings as one sequence so the envelope gets done once, correctly — and we leave your landscaping alive. Licensed and insured, CGC1539072, with two decades of South Florida exteriors behind us.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a pergola or summer kitchen in Sunny Isles Beach?
faqs.a: Almost certainly. Structures, gas lines, electrical, and plumbing all trigger permits with the City of Sunny Isles Beach, and anything with wind exposure needs engineering to High-Velocity Hurricane Zone standards. The upside of the city's digital process is that a complete, well-prepared package moves through review cleanly. We prepare it, file it, and schedule the inspections so you never have to learn the portal exists.

faqs.q: What materials actually survive oceanfront salt air?
faqs.a: Marine-grade stainless for grills and hardware, powder-coated aluminum over raw steel, dense stones and porcelain over porous pavers, and coatings formulated for coastal exposure. A block from the Atlantic, ordinary big-box materials corrode on a schedule you can practically mark on a calendar. Specifying correctly at the start costs somewhat more and is dramatically cheaper than replacing everything in year three.

faqs.q: Can you renovate a balcony or terrace in one of the condo towers?
faqs.a: Balcony slabs, railings, and waterproofing typically belong to the association, not the unit owner, and in the milestone-inspection era many buildings are actively restoring them. What we can do is finish work within the association's rules — flooring systems, summer-kitchen elements where the building allows them, and coordination with any ongoing facade program. We confirm ownership lines and approvals before proposing anything.

faqs.q: When is the best time of year to build outdoors here?
faqs.a: The dry season, roughly November through April, is kindest to concrete, coatings, and schedules, while summer brings daily rain and hurricane-season logistics. The practical move is to start design and permitting months ahead so construction lands in the good window. Plenty of successful projects run through summer anyway — it simply takes a contractor who plans pours and coatings around the weather rather than hoping.

faqs.q: What does a full outdoor-living project cost?
faqs.a: A terrace with a genuine summer kitchen, engineered shade, and new decking is a construction project, not a landscaping line item, and pricing tracks the materials and engineering involved. Wide ranges are honest; precise numbers before a site visit are not. After walking the property we will give you a fixed written price, and we build to it — that is the entire point of hiring us.
